items.question: What is the principal reason to maintain a small expert-labelled eval set alongside a much larger, more cheaply labelled one?

options.A: The small set's labels are authoritative, so it can adjudicate disputes about the large set's labels or the grader validated on them.
options.B: The small set produces narrower confidence intervals on any reported score, because expert labels contain much less noise.
options.C: The small set can be run on every commit, since fewer items means a faster and much cheaper run than the large one.
options.D: The small set avoids the multiple-comparisons problem, because fewer items means fewer significance tests in each report.

items.question: A payments processor compares two prompt versions for dispute-summary generation over 40,000 paired eval items. The versions disagree on 1,200 items: version B is correct on 680 of them and version A on 520, a net gain of 160 items, or 0.4 percentage points. The paired test returns a z of roughly 4.6, well past any conventional threshold. Version B runs on the higher model tier. What should the recommendation to the platform owner be?

options.A: Ship version B: at that significance level the improvement is beyond reasonable doubt, and shipping a proven improvement is the default course of action.
options.B: Reject version B: a 0.4-point gain is well inside normal run-to-run variation on a suite this size, so it is not a real difference.
options.C: Report the gain as real but small, convert 0.4 points into extra correct summaries per month at production volume, and weigh that against the tier cost.
options.D: Re-run the comparison on a smaller and cheaper sample first to confirm the result replicates before committing to a permanent tier change.

items.question: A national archive is building a golden set for a Claude step that assigns subject headings to digitised records. After a full adjudication round, about 7% of items remain genuinely contested: two senior cataloguers each defend a different heading and neither is wrong under the archive's own cataloguing rules. The set will be used to gate releases. What should be done with those items?

options.A: Remove the 7% from the golden set, since an item without a single agreed heading cannot be scored consistently across releases.
options.B: Keep them in a separately reported slice with every defensible heading recorded, accept any of those headings as correct, and treat the slice as a ceiling.
options.C: Assign each contested item the heading chosen by the more senior of the two cataloguers, so that every item carries exactly one agreed reference.
options.D: Run a third senior cataloguer over the contested items and take the majority heading, so a single label always emerges from the process.

items.question: A university's student-services assistant scores 92% on its offline eval suite. A two-week sample of real production conversations, hand-graded against the identical rubric by the same reviewers who wrote it, comes back at 78%. The configurations were confirmed identical. Which explanations are consistent with a gap in that direction? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: The production sample was graded by humans while the eval used a model judge, which necessarily inflates the human-graded figure.
options.B: The eval items were written or tidied by the team, so they are better formed than the messages students actually send.
options.C: The two-week production sample is smaller than the eval set, so its estimate is less precise than the eval's.
options.D: The eval was executed with exactly the same prompt version and generation settings that production is serving.
options.E: Production traffic contains whole categories of request the eval set does not cover, so the worst-handled cases were never scored.

items.question: A task assistant answers some requests and routes others to a human queue rather than attempting them. How should the declined cases be treated when reporting a success rate?

options.A: Exclude them from the denominator, since the system did not attempt those cases and cannot fairly be scored on them.
options.B: Count every declined case as a failure, since the user did not receive an answer from the system itself.
options.C: Count them as successes, since routing to the human queue is the designed behaviour for cases the system should not attempt.
options.D: Report coverage and accuracy-on-attempted as two separate figures, because one combined rate hides the trade between them.

items.question: A car-sharing operator can afford 6,000 judge calls per eval run. The eval lead is choosing between 6,000 distinct items graded once each, and 2,000 items graded three times with a majority verdict. A recent validation found judge–human agreement to be high and the judge's repeat-to-repeat verdicts to be almost always identical. Items, by contrast, vary considerably in difficulty. Which allocation is right, and why?

options.A: 6,000 distinct items: when per-item grading noise is small relative to variation between items, item count is what reduces sampling variance.
options.B: 2,000 items graded three times: majority voting removes grading error, which is the one error source fully under the eval team's control.
options.C: 2,000 items graded three times: a smaller set can be curated far more carefully, and curation quality contributes more to a useful eval than raw count.
options.D: Split the budget: 3,000 items graded once and 1,500 graded twice, hedging against both error sources rather than betting on either one.

items.question: A semiconductor fab introduced a Claude step that drafts equipment-deviation reports; a process engineer reviews and approves every draft before it is filed with quality assurance. The eval scores the drafts against a rubric and reports 88%. The operations director asks whether the feature has improved the quality of the fab's deviation reporting. What should the eval lead do next?

options.A: Report the 88% draft score as the answer, since it is a direct rubric measurement of what the feature itself produces.
options.B: Score reports written by engineers without the assistant against the same rubric, which isolates the model's own contribution to report quality.
options.C: Score the filed report — the artefact after engineer review — against the same rubric, and compare with filed reports from before the feature.
options.D: Measure how heavily engineers edit each draft before approving it, and adopt that edit rate as the feature's quality metric.

items.question: A construction contractor is assembling the first eval set for a Claude step that drafts justifications for variation orders on infrastructure projects. The step has not yet been deployed, so there is no production traffic. Which of the following are sound sources of items for that first set? (Choose THREE.)

options.A: Historical variation orders from the manual process, paired with the justifications the quantity surveyors actually wrote and submitted.
options.B: Outputs the candidate prompt produced during development, retained together with the developing engineer's approve-or-reject decision on each.
options.C: Cases the senior quantity surveyors nominate as the ones most consequential to get wrong, even where those cases are rare.
options.D: The variation orders disputed in the last two years of contract adjudications, since those mark the boundary the drafting has to get right.
options.E: A public benchmark for general business-document summarisation, used to establish a capability floor before task-specific items exist.

items.question: A pipeline post-processes the model's output before a user sees it: trimming, reformatting and inserting the result into a template. Where should the eval's headline quality metric be computed?

options.A: On the raw model output, so that the metric isolates the model's own contribution and is not confounded by later changes to the pipeline.
options.B: On the user-visible artefact, since that carries the quality the metric represents, with raw-output scores kept as a diagnostic.
options.C: On both layers, reported as a single averaged figure so that neither the model nor the pipeline dominates the headline.
options.D: On the raw model output during development to keep the iteration loop fast, and on the finished artefact only at release.

items.question: A rubric has five criteria. What is the argument for asking the judge about them in five separate calls rather than all five in one?

options.A: It lowers total grading cost, because each of the five calls carries a shorter prompt than the combined one.
options.B: It removes the need for anchored level descriptions, because a single criterion asked on its own is unambiguous.
options.C: It makes the grades reproducible, because shorter judge prompts are less sensitive to sampling variation.
options.D: It stops one criterion's verdict from colouring the others, at the cost of more calls and more tokens overall.

items.question: A customs broker's Claude step assigns tariff classifications to shipment descriptions. Its golden set was labelled by two senior classifiers eighteen months ago. Over the last year the pass rate on that set has fallen about five points, spread evenly across three releases whose prompt changes were unrelated formatting adjustments. Hand-review of recent production output by the same classifiers finds no deterioration in quality. The tariff schedule has been amended twice in that period. What is the most likely explanation and the right response?

options.A: Part of the reference is now wrong because the schedule changed; date-stamp labels with the schedule version and re-verify the items the amendments touch.
options.B: The system has regressed despite the formatting-only changes; pin the model version and re-run the earlier releases to confirm where the regression entered.
options.C: The eval set has stopped representing current shipment traffic; resample items from the last year of customs declarations and rebuild the set.
options.D: The judge has drifted over the past year of releases; re-validate the grader against fresh human labels and re-baseline the trend line.

items.question: A facilities-management company gates releases on a 1,000-item eval suite. After the latest release the pass rate fell from 91% to 86%. Investigation shows the 880 pre-existing items still score 91%, exactly as before, while 120 items added to the suite the same week by a different engineer score 49% — which is what pulls the combined figure to 86%. The release is currently blocked. What should the eval lead do next?

options.A: Keep the release blocked and roll back: a five-point drop on the gating suite is a regression by definition and the gate exists precisely to stop this.
options.B: Remove the 120 new items from the gating suite until someone has reviewed them, re-report the 91%, and release as planned.
options.C: Report the two cohorts separately — the release moved nothing on the 880 existing items — and review the 120 new items before they enter the gate.
options.D: Adopt 86% as the new gating baseline, since the enlarged 1,000-item suite represents the task more completely than the old one did.

items.question: A team mirrors live production requests to a candidate Claude configuration running in shadow mode. Which property must the shadow path guarantee for the exercise to be safe?

options.A: Shadow traffic is sampled at the same rate as the canary cohort so the two comparisons are directly interchangeable.
options.B: The shadow path runs at temperature 0 with a fixed seed so its outputs match the production response token for token.
options.C: Shadow responses reach no user or downstream consumer, and any tool the shadow path can reach is read-only or stubbed.
options.D: Shadow requests are billed to a separate account so their spend is excluded from both the production cost baseline and the canary budget.

items.question: A freight brokerage extracts pickup windows, weights and reference numbers from carrier emails with Claude. A 240-case regression suite runs on every pull request and asserts exact string equality on every extracted field; the build fails if any case fails. The suite goes red on roughly one run in four, always on two or three different cases, usually on a free-text address line or a rounded weight. Engineers now re-run the job until it passes. What is the right correction?

options.A: Set temperature to 0 and top_p to 1 for the extraction call, then treat any remaining run-to-run variation as a vendor-side model defect.
options.B: Gate on a suite-level field-accuracy threshold calibrated to measured run-to-run variation, keeping exact assertions only for fields where any deviation is a defect.
options.C: Quarantine every intermittently failing case into a non-blocking flaky list so the gate stays green, and triage that list at the monthly engineering review.
options.D: Record and replay the model responses for all 240 cases so the suite becomes fully deterministic, refreshing the recordings at each release.

items.question: A hospital network's clinician-facing assistant answers questions over internal care protocols using RAG. The offline suite reports faithfulness 0.94 and answer relevance 0.90, both computed reference-free against the retrieved context. Clinicians report answers that are confidently wrong, and in two cases omitted a contraindication. Investigation finds the index contains both current and superseded revisions of several protocols. Which TWO conclusions are best supported? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: An answer grounded in a retrieved but superseded revision satisfies faithfulness, so a score of 0.94 is fully consistent with the errors clinicians are reporting.
options.B: The high faithfulness score isolates the generator as the weak component, so the retrieval stage can be excluded from the investigation.
options.C: Answer relevance asks only whether the response addresses the question that was asked, so a response that omits a contraindication can still score highly.
options.D: Reference-free faithfulness and answer relevance together bound answer correctness against ground truth, so the offline suite is adequate and the problem must be in the serving layer.
options.E: Context precision would have caught this, because a superseded revision is by definition an irrelevant chunk and is penalised by that metric.

items.question: A telco canaries a new system prompt for its billing-dispute assistant at 5% of traffic. Automated rollback is wired to three signals: p95 latency, HTTP error rate, and an LLM-judge quality score computed by a nightly batch job. Four hours into the canary, containment — disputes resolved without handoff to a human agent — falls from 62% to 51% in the canary arm. No rollback fires, and the drop is noticed the next morning by an operations analyst. What is the primary defect in the canary design?

options.A: The rollback criteria omit the business outcome the canary existed to protect, and its only quality signal refreshes nightly, not within the decision window.
options.B: A 5% cohort yields too few disputes per hour to detect an eleven-point move, so the canary needed at least a 25% allocation before automation could act.
options.C: The comparison should have been run as a shadow deployment, which would have surfaced the containment drop without exposing any customer to the new prompt.
options.D: Automated rollback is inappropriate for prompt changes; an on-call engineer should review the canary dashboards hourly and roll back by hand if a signal moves.

items.question: In RAG evaluation, what does context recall capture that context precision does not?

options.A: Whether the retrieved chunks are ordered so that the most relevant appear at the top of the context window.
options.B: Whether the generated answer asserts only claims that are supported by the retrieved chunks.
options.C: Whether the retrieved set is free of near-duplicate chunks drawn from the same source document.
options.D: Whether the evidence needed to produce the reference answer was actually present in the retrieved set.

items.question: An insurer's claims-triage agent uses Claude with six tools, two of which are write operations: verify_identity and authorise_interim_payment. The team's eval scores only the final triage decision and reports 93% on a 500-case set. Post-incident review of three production complaints finds the agent reached the correct triage decision each time, but in all three had called authorise_interim_payment before any successful identity verification. The eval scored all three as passes. Which change to the eval most directly closes this gap?

options.A: Add step-level assertions over the recorded trajectory that fail any run breaking a tool precondition, scored independently of the final decision.
options.B: Raise the final-answer pass threshold from 93% to 98% and require two consecutive clean runs, so borderline agent behaviour no longer clears the gate.
options.C: Compare each run's full tool-call sequence against a reference trajectory recorded from an approved run, and fail any case whose sequence does not match exactly.
options.D: Expand the eval set with four hundred more cases drawn from the claim types the three complaints came from, weighted toward interim-payment scenarios.

items.question: A specialty retailer is A/B testing two system prompts for its product-advice assistant, with conversion to purchase as the primary metric. The experiment framework assigns an arm independently on each API request; sessions average six turns. After two weeks the two arms' conversion rates are statistically indistinguishable, and the growth team proposes running for another four weeks to reach significance. What should you do first?

options.A: Extend the run as proposed, since conversion is a low-rate metric and the confidence interval will narrow with more sessions.
options.B: Raise the allocation from the current split to 50/50 so both arms accumulate sessions at the maximum rate the platform allows.
options.C: Restart with sticky assignment at the session or user level, and discard the existing data as uninterpretable.
options.D: Replace conversion with an LLM-judge score over sampled transcripts, which will reach significance on far fewer sessions.

items.question: A government benefits agency runs a Claude-based eligibility assistant. An incident review finds that text a claimant typed into a free-form circumstances field caused the assistant to disclose the internal scoring thresholds used to prioritise applications. A prompt fix has shipped and been verified by hand. The safety lead asks how to guarantee the behaviour cannot return in a later release. What should the team institute?

options.A: Add the exact input string to the input filter's blocklist so any future occurrence is rejected with a generic refusal before it reaches the model.
options.B: Add the incident input and a family of paraphrases and structural variants to the pre-deploy safety suite as blocking cases with a tracked pass rate.
options.C: Add the incident input to the nightly advisory eval and review the disclosure-category trend with the safety lead at the monthly forum.
options.D: Commission a quarterly external red-team engagement whose scope explicitly includes disclosure of internal scoring thresholds and prioritisation logic.

items.question: Which criterion is most defensible as a hard blocking gate on a deployment pipeline for a Claude-based feature?

options.A: A measurable improvement in the mean helpfulness score over the currently deployed release.
options.B: Mean output length within ten percent of the currently deployed release.
options.C: No regression against the previous release on a protected set of safety and policy cases.
options.D: A perfect pass rate on every case in the complete functional eval suite.

items.question: A streaming media company gates prompt changes for its content-metadata tagger on a 600-case suite. The gate fails the build if any case flips from pass to fail versus the stored results of the last release. Most candidate changes now fail on four to nine flipped cases while also fixing a similar number, and reviewers routinely override the gate. An engineer proposes simply allowing up to ten flips. What is the sounder redesign?

options.A: Re-run the incumbent alongside the candidate in the same job and fail only when the candidate's net regression exceeds the incumbent-versus-incumbent flip count.
options.B: Allow up to ten flips as proposed, and retune that allowance each quarter from the number of overrides reviewers issued in the previous one.
options.C: Keep the stored results from the last three releases as separate baselines, and fail a case only when it fails against all three of them.
options.D: Replace per-case pass/fail with a continuous judge score and fail the build if the suite mean drops at all against the last release.

items.question: A utility's field-engineer assistant handles about 30,000 queries a day across outage triage, asset lookup and safety-procedure questions. New test cases are currently created only from sessions where a user pressed thumbs-down, which happens in 0.4% of sessions. The quality lead wants both to discover failure modes nobody has thought of and to know how often each one actually occurs. Which TWO changes best serve those two goals? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Review a random sample of sessions on a fixed cadence, stratified by query type and region, regardless of whether any feedback was left.
options.B: Make the thumbs-down control more prominent in the interface so a larger share of dissatisfied users report, increasing the volume of review candidates.
options.C: Promote every thumbs-down session automatically into the blocking pre-deploy regression suite once it has been de-identified.
options.D: Score all traffic with an LLM judge against the existing quality rubric and treat the lowest-scoring sessions as the discovery mechanism.
options.E: Embed production queries, cluster them, and direct review effort at clusters that are thinly represented in the current test set.

items.question: A law firm's contract-review assistant ingests counterparty PDFs supplied by the opposing side, retrieves clauses from them, and can call two tools: flag_for_partner and email_summary, the latter sending to addresses in the matter record. The security team's adversarial suite consists of 400 attack strings placed in the user message, and reports zero successful attacks over the last three releases. Which gap in the suite matters most?

options.A: The suite does not test multi-turn escalation, where an attacker builds up context across several user messages before making the request.
options.B: The suite contains only English-language attack strings, so the same jailbreaks translated or transliterated into another language go unmeasured.
options.C: The suite scores refusal but never records response latency or token spend, so prompt-driven denial-of-service attacks would go unnoticed.
options.D: No attack is placed in the counterparty document content, which reaches the model in the same context as its instructions alongside a send-capable tool.

items.question: An answer-relevance metric flags a response in a RAG eval run. What has it most likely detected?

options.A: The response asserts something that the retrieved chunks do not support.
options.B: The response is evasive, drifts off topic, or answers only part of what was asked.
options.C: The retrieval stage failed to return a document that the reference answer depends on.
options.D: The response contradicts the ground-truth answer stored with the eval case.

items.question: A manufacturer wants to shadow-test a new version of its maintenance triage agent against mirrored production traffic. The agent has four tools: read_sensor_history and lookup_part are reads; create_work_order writes to the CMMS; page_technician sends a pager notification. Which THREE controls are required before mirroring begins? (Choose THREE.)

options.A: Route the shadow agent behind a 5% canary cohort so only that small group of technicians sees its output if it misbehaves.
options.B: Replace create_work_order and page_technician with sandboxed stubs that log the intended call and return synthetic results.
options.C: Require shadow and production outputs to be token-identical at temperature 0 before any comparison is treated as valid.
options.D: Ensure no shadow output reaches any downstream consumer, including caches, analytics events and queues production also writes to.
options.E: Provision and monitor the additional inference spend and read-tool load that duplicating live traffic creates.

items.question: An edtech company's eval suite for its tutoring assistant is 1,800 cases, takes about 35 minutes of wall clock, and costs roughly a day of production inference spend per run. It currently runs on every push; the team pushes around 30 times a day and the eval bill now exceeds the product's serving bill. Leadership wants the cost down without losing pre-release assurance. Which design best achieves that?

options.A: Move the full suite to a weekly scheduled run and rely on review of the prompt diff at pull request time to catch regressions in between.
options.B: Run a stratified subset including the whole safety set on every push, the full suite at merge and before release, and the full suite nightly against main.
options.C: Cut the suite to 300 cases by dropping every case that has passed on the last twenty consecutive runs, keeping the ones that still fail sometimes.
options.D: Cache model responses keyed by a hash of the rendered prompt so repeated runs cost nothing, refreshing the cache on the first of each month.

items.question: An online travel agency canaries a model swap for its itinerary-change assistant at 10% of traffic for five days. Aggregate judge quality and p95 latency are flat and cost per task falls 22%. Preparing the ramp to 100%, an analyst slices the canary data and finds that for non-English sessions — 7% of traffic — the escalation-to-human rate rose from 4% to 11%. The team asks to proceed. What is the appropriate next step?

options.A: Proceed to 100%, since aggregate quality held and a 22% cost saving is material, and add the non-English segment to the production dashboard.
options.B: Roll back the model swap and stay on the incumbent, since a seven-point escalation regression on any customer segment disqualifies the change.
options.C: Hold the ramp and re-run the canary with language as a pre-registered guardrail powered for that segment, or ramp only the passing segments.
options.D: Treat the finding as a multiple-comparisons artefact given how many segments could have been sliced, apply a Bonferroni correction, and continue the ramp.

items.question: A gaming platform maintains an adversarial suite of 900 prompts across nine harm categories for the assistant that helps moderators draft enforcement notices. Results are reported to leadership as a single number — 97% blocked — and the release gate requires at least 95%. The trust and safety director asks whether this gate is fit for purpose. What is the main weakness?

options.A: One category can fail outright while the aggregate still clears 95%; the gate needs per-category rates with severity-weighted floors instead.
options.B: Nine hundred prompts is too small a sample for a safety claim, and the suite should be expanded by an order of magnitude before it gates anything.
options.C: The suite is static across releases, so the gate should be regenerated from scratch each time to stop prompts being tuned against known attack strings.
options.D: The threshold is too low for a safety control, and raising the aggregate floor from 95% to 99% blocked would give the gate real teeth.

items.question: A pharmaceutical company runs adverse-event narrative summarisation on a specific pinned Claude model version, validated and documented under its model risk management process; the regulator expects documented evidence supporting any change to a validated system. A newer model becomes available and the product team wants its lower latency. The validation suite is locked and version-controlled. Which approach lets the team move while preserving the assurance the process requires?

options.A: Move the configuration to a floating alias so the system tracks the newest model automatically, and rely on production quality monitoring to detect any degradation.
options.B: Accept the vendor's published evaluation results for the newer model as the evidence, since capability claims about the model are the vendor's to make.
options.C: Run an online A/B between the two versions on live adverse-event traffic, adopt whichever wins on the judge score, and file that comparison as the evidence.
options.D: Run the locked suite against both versions on identical inputs, document the paired deltas including the safety subset, and ship it as a versioned release.

items.question: In a canary release or online experiment, what distinguishes a guardrail metric from the primary metric?

options.A: It is the same metric as the primary, measured on a smaller cohort so that early movement is visible sooner.
options.B: It is a secondary metric used to break the tie when the primary metric comes back inconclusive at the end of the planned run.
options.C: It is computed offline before deployment, whereas the primary metric is only observable in live traffic.
options.D: It is a metric the change is not expected to improve, watched so a win on the primary cannot be bought by degrading it.

items.question: A food-delivery marketplace runs two experiments concurrently on its order-support assistant. Team A tests a rewritten system prompt; team B tests a new retrieval configuration. Each randomises users independently, so users land in all four combinations. Both report a clear win on the same primary metric, and each was later re-confirmed on its own in a separate single-change canary. When both changes are deployed together, the metric returns to its pre-experiment level. What is the most likely explanation and the right correction?

options.A: The two randomisations were correlated, so each analysis was contaminated by the other; assign both experiments from a shared hash so the four arms are orthogonal.
options.B: Both original wins were false positives produced by repeatedly checking the results during the run; adopt a fixed-horizon analysis and re-test each change.
options.C: The changes interact, so each single-change estimate holds only while the other is absent; analyse the four cells factorially and test the pair as its own arm.
options.D: The initial wins were novelty effects that decayed once users adapted to the new behaviour; extend future experiments until the weekly effect stabilises.

items.question: A port operator plans a two-week shadow run of a candidate configuration for its vessel-arrival exception assistant. All requests are mirrored, write tools are stubbed, and shadow responses are discarded. Which TWO questions can the run answer directly? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Whether duty operators accept the candidate's recommendations more often than the incumbent's.
options.B: Whether the candidate's p95 end-to-end response time meets the team's four-second budget on the real production input mix.
options.C: Whether the candidate reduces the rate at which exceptions are escalated to the duty manager.
options.D: Whether the candidate satisfies the operator's record-keeping obligation, since shadow runs write to the same audit log as production.
options.E: How the candidate's cost per request compares with the incumbent's over the same two weeks of traffic.

items.question: An enterprise software vendor runs an IT service-desk agent that resolves access requests. After a prompt change shipped, final-answer accuracy is unchanged at 91% and user satisfaction is flat, but monthly inference spend rose 38% and p95 resolution time went from 22 to 51 seconds. Inspection shows the agent now re-queries the directory tool several times per ticket where it used to query once. The eval harness already records complete trajectories but scores only the final answer. What should be added to the release gate to catch this class of change in future?

options.A: Assert a maximum wall-clock duration of 30 seconds per eval case in the harness, so any agent that runs slower than that fails the build.
options.B: Gate per-case trajectory counters — tool calls, duplicate calls with identical arguments, tokens per resolved case — against the incumbent's distribution.
options.C: Expand the final-answer eval set until accuracy is estimated to within a point, so that small quality shifts around the 91% figure become detectable.
options.D: Add a judge over the final response scoring conciseness and redundancy, since verbose answers are the usual driver of token growth on a service desk.

items.question: An HR software vendor maintains an adversarial suite whose cases include attack strings that previously succeeded in making its assistant surface another tenant's data. The safety team wants the suite to run on every release build in the normal CI pipeline, which all 200 engineers can read. How should the corpus and its results be handled?

options.A: Commit the corpus alongside the application code so any engineer can add cases, on the grounds that attacks of this kind are already publicly discussed.
options.B: Store only irreversible hashes of the attack strings in the repository and have the job compare hashes at run time, so the literal text is never checked in.
options.C: Keep the corpus in an access-restricted store, fetch it with a scoped credential at run time, and emit only per-category pass rates.
options.D: Remove the suite from CI entirely and run it as a manual pre-release exercise operated by two safety engineers on an isolated, air-gapped workstation.

items.question: An agricultural co-operative runs a nightly eval on the main branch of its agronomy advisory assistant. Tonight the suite score falls from 0.88 to 0.71. Since the last green run, three commits merged — a prompt edit, a retrieval filter change, and a logging change — and the platform team also repointed the service's internal model alias to a newer tier the same evening. What is the correct first action?

options.A: Re-run tonight's suite on the same commit with the model alias pinned back to the version the last green run used, isolating the model change.
options.B: Bisect the three merged commits by re-running the suite with each reverted in turn, starting with the prompt edit as the most likely cause.
options.C: Revert all three commits, confirm the suite returns to 0.88, and then re-land them one at a time over the following three nightly runs.
options.D: Re-run the suite twice more before investigating, since a single nightly figure fluctuates and a seventeen-point drop may not reproduce on the same commit.

items.question: A public transit authority's rider-support assistant answers from a 60,000-document corpus of policies and timetables, retrieving the top 20 chunks per query. The eval reports context recall 0.93, context precision 0.41, faithfulness 0.88, answer relevance 0.86. Human reviewers say the answers usually contain a correct core plus one or two confidently stated conditions that belong to a different route or a different fare zone. What does this metric pattern indicate, and what should the next eval measure?

options.A: Faithfulness at 0.88 shows the generator is fabricating the extra conditions; tighten the grounding instruction and re-measure faithfulness on the same set.
options.B: Low precision alongside high recall is the expected shape for large-k retrieval and is harmless, since the generator ignores irrelevant context; push recall toward 0.99.
options.C: The chunks are too small to carry a complete condition, which is what depresses precision; the next eval should sweep chunk size against answer correctness.
options.D: The evidence is present but heavily diluted and the generator is pulling in adjacent material; sweep k downward, tracking precision, correctness and lost recall.

items.question: Which failure mode is structurally invisible to an evaluation that scores only an agent's final answer?

options.A: An answer that reads fluently but states a fact the source record contradicts.
options.B: An answer that violates the JSON schema the downstream service requires of every payload.
options.C: A run that reaches the right answer after an unauthorised or wasteful intermediate step.
options.D: An answer that arrives after the caller's request timeout has already elapsed.

items.question: What should be true before a team advances a canary to its next ramp step?

options.A: The current step has run for the calendar duration fixed in the rollout plan, regardless of how much traffic it received.
options.B: Every guardrail has enough exposure at this step to be judged against its threshold, and all are within it.
options.C: The primary metric shows a statistically significant improvement over the control at the current ramp step.
options.D: The candidate has produced no errors of any kind at the current step — no 5xx responses and no failed tool calls.

items.question: A health insurer is standing up an ongoing red-team programme against its member-services assistant, which retrieves plan documents and can call a claims-status tool. The CISO's complaint about the previous ad-hoc effort is that its output was a slide of anecdotes with no way to tell whether the system was getting safer. Which THREE practices most directly make the programme's output measurable across releases? (Choose THREE.)

options.A: Retire an attack from the corpus once the system has blocked it in two consecutive runs, keeping the suite focused on the unsolved weaknesses.
options.B: Record the model version, prompt version and guardrail configuration with every run, so a change in results is attributable to a known difference.
options.C: Fix the scope and the number of attempts per harm category before each engagement, so a zero-success category reflects coverage rather than effort.
options.D: Score the programme on the count of novel attacks discovered per engagement, to keep the team incentivised toward creative coverage of the taxonomy.
options.E: Execute every attack end to end against the deployed stack, recording whether a guardrail intercepted it and whether the model itself complied.

items.question: Why should a RAG regression suite that gates application code changes run against a pinned corpus snapshot rather than the live index?

options.A: Because otherwise a score movement cannot be attributed — index content churn and the code change under test are confounded.
options.B: Because querying the live index from CI adds retrieval load that competes with production traffic at peak hours.
options.C: Because embedding vectors drift over time, and a snapshot keeps the stored vectors numerically stable from one run to the next.
options.D: Because documents added after the eval set was authored may not have been reviewed for use in a test environment.

items.question: A telehealth provider A/B tests replacing Sonnet with Haiku for its symptom-intake summariser. Assignment is sticky at the clinician level across about forty clinicians, and the primary metric is edits per summary over four weeks. Median response time in the treatment arm falls from 6.1 to 2.4 seconds. Which TWO threats to the comparison should be resolved before the result is acted on? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Sticky assignment invalidates the randomisation, because each of the forty clinicians contributes many correlated observations to one arm only.
options.B: The result cannot be read unless edits are normalised by summary length, since the two tiers produce summaries of very different average lengths.
options.C: With only about forty clinicians, differences in individual editing habits can swamp the treatment effect unless assignment is stratified or a pre-period baseline is used as a covariate.
options.D: A two-second response instead of a six-second one changes how clinicians work through the summary, so edits per summary captures latency as well as quality.
options.E: Behavioural metrics such as edits per summary require at least a full quarter of exposure before any model comparison can be interpreted at all.

items.question: A test suite replays previously recorded model responses instead of calling the API. What does such a suite still verify?

options.A: The deterministic code around the model — output parsing, schema validation, tool dispatch and retries.
options.B: That the current prompt still elicits the expected refusal and formatting behaviour from the model in use.
options.C: That switching to a newer model version has not degraded the output quality on these cases.
options.D: That the live retrieval stage still returns the chunks that the reference answers depend on.

items.question: A carmaker's owner-app assistant has been live for eighteen months. To refresh its eval, the team samples 500 recent production conversations, has them labelled, and measures 0.94 — against 0.81 on the two-year-old set built before launch. Support-ticket volume in the assistant's topic areas is unchanged over the same period, and the team is preparing to retire the old set. What is the most likely explanation for the gap?

options.A: The assistant genuinely improved over eighteen months of iteration, and the older set over-weights defects that were fixed in its first few months.
options.B: Production traffic has adapted — users reformulate what fails and stop asking what it cannot do — so a sample under-represents the failures that remain.
options.C: Recent traffic is drawn from a narrower seasonal window, so the new set covers fewer distinct intents than the pre-launch set did.
options.D: The new cases were drawn after the fixes were made, so they were effectively part of development and can no longer measure generalisation.

items.question: A pharmacy chain's adversarial run reports 40 of 40 attacks blocked for its patient-messaging assistant. Reading the traces, the safety engineer sees that in 31 cases an input classifier rejected the request and the model was never invoked; in the remaining 9 the model itself declined. Leadership is being told the assistant is fully resistant in this category. What should the engineer do next?

options.A: Report the 40 of 40 result as it stands, since from the patient's perspective the system did block every attempt in this harm category.
options.B: Tighten the input classifier so that it also catches the 9 attacks that reached the model, making the outer layer the single point of enforcement.
options.C: Re-run the suite in a non-production environment with the input classifier disabled, and record both layers' refusal rates separately.
options.D: Remove the input classifier, since the model refused unaided in the cases that reached it and the extra hop adds latency and false positives.

items.question: Which TWO practices most directly make a failing eval run in CI attributable to the change under test? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Pin the model version the job uses rather than resolving a floating alias at run time.
options.B: Re-run the job automatically up to three times and report the best of the three results.
options.C: Raise the job's concurrency so the suite finishes sooner and developers see the result while the change is fresh.
options.D: Record the prompt template version, corpus snapshot id and eval-set version in the run artefact alongside the score.
options.E: Run the job only against the merge commit, never against the branch head.

items.question: A hotel group fixes a system prompt to correct date-format errors in booking-change requests. On the 120-case date-handling set the candidate scores 0.96 against a 0.74 baseline, and the team proposes shipping on that evidence alone. The assistant also handles cancellations, loyalty queries and group bookings from the same system prompt. What must the gate additionally require?

options.A: A non-regression run over the rest of the suite, covering the other capabilities that are driven by the same system prompt.
options.B: Evidence that the improvement on the date set is statistically significant rather than a sampling artefact of 120 cases.
options.C: A 1% canary for twenty-four hours, on the basis that live booking traffic will surface anything the offline suite missed.
options.D: Human review of twenty sampled outputs from the date-handling set, to confirm the automated score reflects a real improvement.

items.question: A customs brokerage runs a tariff-classification agent with eight tools; runs take between three and fifteen steps, and several orderings are legitimate for the same shipment. The team has 400 eval cases and wants trajectory scoring that tells them why runs fail, without a maintenance burden that grows every time a tool is added. Which scoring design is most sustainable?

options.A: Author a reference trajectory for each of the 400 cases and score every run by edit distance between the recorded run and its reference.
options.B: Score each case against order-and-precondition assertions plus required-call and forbidden-call sets, leaving unconstrained steps unscored.
options.C: Have a judge read each full trajectory and rate its reasonableness on a five-point scale, gating the release on the mean rating.
options.D: Gate on the step count alone against a per-case maximum, on the grounds that runs which wander are the ones that end up wrong.

items.question: Why should an adversarial test suite include benign prompts that superficially resemble attacks?

options.A: To prevent the model from inferring that every case in the run is hostile and refusing on that basis.
options.B: To exercise the guardrail classifier's throughput under a realistic mix of accepted and rejected traffic at peak load times.
options.C: To measure over-refusal, so hardening that buys a higher block rate by rejecting legitimate requests shows up as a cost.
options.D: To supply the negative examples needed to fit the input classifier's decision threshold before release.

items.question: An international NGO's donor-services assistant answers questions over grant agreements and disbursement policies. Its eval set is 300 real questions harvested from the support inbox, with no reference answers; the team currently reports faithfulness, answer relevance and context precision, all judged from the question, the retrieved chunks and the response. The head of engineering asks for context recall to be added. What does that require?

options.A: Nothing new — recall is computed from the question and retrieved chunks the same way precision is, so it runs on the existing job.
options.B: Ground truth per question: a reference answer, or the passages that must be retrieved for it to be answerable.
options.C: Human relevance ratings for each retrieved chunk, so that irrelevant chunks can be excluded from the denominator.
options.D: A larger retrieval k of 20 or more, so that recall has headroom to be measured across the full 300-question set.

items.question: An online marketplace is preparing to canary a new version of its dispute-resolution agent, which can issue refunds up to a per-case ceiling without human approval. The rollout plan specifies a 5% cohort with automatic rollback that reroutes all traffic to the incumbent within sixty seconds of any guardrail breach. The risk lead says the plan does not bound the exposure. What is the substance of that objection, and what should the design add?

options.A: Sixty seconds is too slow for an action that moves money; the rollback automation should trigger within ten seconds of the first guardrail breach.
options.B: A canary is inappropriate for any change touching money; the candidate should run in shadow mode with refunds stubbed until confidence is established.
options.C: The guardrail set omits refund rate and refund value; adding both as automated rollback triggers bounds the exposure the risk lead is describing.
options.D: Rerouting does not undo refunds already issued, so the canary must bound effects too: low-value disputes only, a cap on cumulative refund authority, and reconciliation.

items.question: An airline's disruption-rebooking assistant logs complete traces for every session. The quality team can review about 200 sessions a week by hand and wants to maximise the number of previously unseen failure modes it finds. Which TWO log signals are the most productive filters for that review queue? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Sessions from the highest-volume one percent of travellers, who exercise the assistant most heavily across all its intents.
options.B: Sessions with the largest retrieved context payload, measured in tokens across all the chunks retrieved for the session.
options.C: Sessions in which the traveller rephrased essentially the same request three or more times in succession.
options.D: Sessions with the shortest generation latency, which indicates the model produced its answer with very little work.
options.E: Sessions where the assistant returned its scripted fallback response and the traveller carried on typing afterwards.

items.question: A meal-kit subscription company wants to A/B two prompts for the assistant that handles cancellation conversations. The outcome the business cares about is 60-day churn. A contractual platform migration forces a decision in three weeks, and that deadline cannot move. Which approach gives the soundest basis for the decision?

options.A: Choose a leading indicator observable inside three weeks, verify on historical data that it predicts 60-day churn, and decide on it.
options.B: Run the experiment for three weeks measuring 60-day churn and pick whichever arm is ahead on the cohorts that have matured by then.
options.C: Replace the outcome metric with an LLM-judge score of conversation quality, which reaches a stable estimate within a few days.
options.D: Run the experiment for nine weeks so the primary metric is fully observed, and defer the migration decision until the churn figure reads out.

items.question: A field-service software vendor ships one assistant to 600 tenants. Each tenant supplies its own glossary, contributes a tenant-specific block to the system prompt, and toggles three optional tools on or off. The regression suite runs against the vendor's demo tenant and has been green for eight months, yet almost every release produces two or three tenant-specific incidents in the first week. What is the right change to the testing approach?

options.A: Deepen the demo-tenant suite with several hundred additional cases covering the workflows the recent tenant incidents touched.
options.B: Require each tenant to run an acceptance pass against a staging copy of their own configuration before their upgrade window is scheduled.
options.C: Run the suite over a matrix of representative configurations spanning the axes that actually vary: tenant prompt blocks, tool toggles and glossary shapes.
options.D: Standardise the tenant prompt blocks into a fixed set of vendor-authored options, so that all 600 tenants run one of a handful of prompts the vendor has validated.

items.question: A consumer messaging app's safety team reads a newly published write-up of a technique reported to defeat content policies across assistant products generally. Their own assistant sits behind an input classifier and a system-prompt policy, and has an established harm taxonomy and adversarial suite. Product management asks whether to ship an emergency system-prompt change tonight. What should the team do first?

options.A: Ship a defensive instruction into the system prompt tonight, then measure its effect on the adversarial suite over the following few days of runs.
options.B: Reproduce the technique against their own system in an isolated environment, across the harm taxonomy, to establish where they are affected.
options.C: Add the published example strings to the input classifier's blocklist so copies of the technique are rejected before reaching the model.
options.D: Wait for the model provider to mitigate the technique, since the write-up describes it as general to assistant products.

items.question: A title insurance company is changing the retrieval configuration behind the assistant its underwriters use to answer policy-exception questions. The company already has an annotated evidence set, a pinned eval corpus, and entitlement fixtures covering the access rules that govern which files each underwriter may see. Which THREE checks belong in the blocking gate for this change? (Choose THREE.)

options.A: Context recall against the annotated evidence set does not regress relative to the incumbent.
options.B: No query returns a passage the requesting user is not entitled to see, verified across the entitlement fixtures.
options.C: Mean number of retrieved chunks per query stays within ten percent of the incumbent configuration.
options.D: Faithfulness and human-judged correctness on the pinned eval set do not regress relative to the incumbent.
options.E: Answer relevance improves over the incumbent by a statistically significant margin.

items.question: A news publisher shadow-ran a candidate summariser for two weeks across 1.4 million mirrored article requests. Sixty-one percent of shadow outputs differ textually from what production returned. The team has capacity for roughly 300 human comparisons and wants to find failure modes the candidate introduces that the offline suite did not contain. How should the 300 be selected?

options.A: Draw a simple random sample of 300 from the 850,000 differing outputs, so the review is an unbiased picture of the candidate's behaviour.
options.B: Review the 300 pairs with the greatest textual distance between the candidate and the production output, measured by a token-level diff.
options.C: Review the 300 candidate outputs with the lowest automated quality scores in the candidate arm, without looking at the production pair.
options.D: Screen the differences with automated checks for entity and figure mismatches, schema violations and safety flags, then cluster and sample across clusters.

items.question: Why should an eval harness report a case that errored — a timeout, a throttling response, a tool outage — separately from a case the system answered incorrectly?

options.A: Because errored cases should count as passes, given that the model itself was never at fault for a timeout or a tool outage.
options.B: Because throttling responses indicate the harness is running too many cases concurrently and the suite should be resized to fit the provider's rate limit.
options.C: Because folding infrastructure failures into the quality score makes the gate depend on transient conditions that can mask or mimic a regression.
options.D: Because error counts are the operational metric leadership tracks and therefore belong on a different dashboard from quality.

items.question: A recruitment platform's candidate-screening agent passed a 300-case evaluation at 95% and shipped. In production, about 2% of runs consume the entire step budget; traces show the agent alternating between two tools when a candidate record is missing a required field, until the budget is exhausted and the run is killed. The eval set was assembled from complete, well-formed records. Which change to the team's evaluation most directly stops this class of defect from shipping again?

options.A: Add cases built from degraded inputs — missing fields, empty tool results, tool errors — and assert bounded steps, no repeated call, explicit escalation.
options.B: Reduce the per-run step budget so that runs which fail to converge are cut off much earlier, capping the cost of the 2% that currently loop.
options.C: Add a loop detector to the orchestrator that aborts any run that repeats an identical tool call with identical arguments three times.
options.D: Grow the eval set to a thousand records sampled from the same population, so that rare behaviours have a chance to appear.

items.question: A marketplace A/B tests two prompts for the assistant that drafts content-moderation decisions. Listings are randomised between arms, both arms' drafts flow into a single human reviewer queue, and reviewers work the queue unlabelled as to arm. The primary metrics are reviewer approval rate and time-to-decision. What most threatens the validity of the comparison?

options.A: Reviewers are blinded to the arm, so they cannot calibrate their judgement to the version that produced the draft in front of them.
options.B: The arms interfere through the shared queue and reviewer pool, so one arm's drafts change the conditions under which the other's are handled.
options.C: Randomising per listing is too fine-grained; assignment should be at the seller level to keep a seller's listings consistent.
options.D: Approval rate is unsuitable as a primary metric because reviewers approve the large majority of drafts either way, leaving very little headroom.
